architecture: v3 (re-root 2026-11-01: the Arafura Examinations Board's decision whether Question 6 of its 2026 Senior Certificate History Paper 2 is scaled before the grade boundaries are applied, read from the candidates who answered all three optional essays)
slot_note: batch 1 re-root; architecture 1 (quantitative finance, the 13F holdings carry) failed the portal's determinism block, architecture 2 (record linkage of heat deaths) was sent back at its stage 4 judge on Gate H3
niche: an Australian not-for-profit examinations board's senior-certificate History paper on which candidates answer two of three optional essay questions, deciding before results whether the essay its candidates find hardest is scaled, which only the candidates who answered all three essays (marked in full, the best two credited) show without the choice in it
answer: Scale Question 6: raise every candidate's mark on it by 2 marks before the best two essays are credited and the boundaries are applied (Questions 4 and 5 unchanged)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field and the board's code of practice correctly compares each optional question's marks with the others for the candidates who answered it, adjusting for their Section A marks or within the candidates who answered it beside another, finds Question 6 well under a mark and a half harder and files no scaling; candidates chose Question 6 by knowing its topic, so every comparison among its choosers carries that knowledge, and the candidates who answered all three essays, who chose nothing, put it over two marks harder, so its marks are scaled up.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is an optional question's demand for the paper's candidates, the examinee-choice problem of test equating (making marks earned on different chosen questions comparable before one set of grade boundaries is applied); with wards or loans for essay questions there is no rubric choice, no topic a candidate chooses by and no marking of every attempt, so the task stops making sense.
layer1: a marking export with one row per marking event, re-marks as later rows
marks timestamped in UTC from markers in five time zones
candidate numbers reissued when a candidate moved centre
an uncredited flag on the answers past the rubric
absent candidates and withdrawn scripts as zero-mark rows
Section A from the scanning system under its own question codes
post-results reviews logged in UTC, one request covering several components
centre codes changed at a 2025 merger of two school groups
stakeholder_role: the board's executive, on the Head of Research and Standards' paper before results are certified

spine.entity: a marking event on one candidate's answer to one Paper 2 essay question

world.geography: Australia (a fictional not-for-profit examinations board in Darwin examining schools across Australia, the Pacific and South-East Asia)
world.org_type: a not-for-profit examinations board that sets, marks and awards a senior school certificate

driver: The decisive quantity is how demanding one optional item is against the others for the whole population, and each unit took the optional items it chose by a private advantage on them; every comparison among choosers (their means, an adjustment for a compulsory measure, the differences within units that took two) carries that advantage, and only the units that took every optional item compare them with no choice in it.
driver_concrete: Question 6's demand is read from the candidates who answered all three optional essays, whose differences within the candidate carry no choice, because the candidates who chose Question 6 knew its topic, so its choosers' marks hide its demand in their means, in a Section A adjustment and in their own pairs of answers alike.
stump: A competent analyst compares Question 6's marks with the other optional questions' for the candidates who answered it, adjusting for Section A or within the candidates who answered it beside another essay, finds it well under the code's mark and a half harder and files no scaling; the step that lands it there is reading demand from choosers, when the candidates who chose Question 6 knew its topic, and the candidates who answered all three essays put it over two marks harder, so its marks are scaled up by two.

differentiation.task238: task238 reads a reporting channel's effect through a randomised nudge (the arms' difference over the uptake difference); here nothing is assigned, and the comparison is the units that took every option and so chose none
differentiation.task233: task233 carries a missing-value departure measured on a gold-standard follow-up across base rates; here no value is missing and no follow-up exists, the bias is the choosers' own advantage on the option they chose
differentiation.task256: task256 carries a reference group's joint distribution of several measurements to a population; here the comparison is within the same units' own answers, with no reference group
differentiation.task262: task262 carries a noise reliability from a subsample selected on its level; here selection is on a private advantage for each option, and the units that chose no option remove it
differentiation.task267: task267 weights a two-phase reference check by its sampling fractions; here no sampling design exists, only the units that answered every option
differentiation.task273: task273's lineage reads a group's event rate from uninvolved parties drawn where events are frequent; here no exposure is measured and no second party exists
differentiation.task280: task280 corrects probes that the members' own activity silences; here every answer is marked in full and nothing under-samples
differentiation.task465: task465 fuses two traits held in different sources through a small source holding both; here one property of one option is read inside the units, from a single marking record
differentiation.task473: task473 completes positives an observer noticed by the notice share measured where everyone is tested; here every answer is observed and the bias is the choice of option itself
differentiation.task54: task54 multiplies a per-event loss over the units in custody under a recovered rule; here no rule is recovered and nothing is in custody

lineage.fate: in-house round 2 missed at flat carry; in-house round 3 (2026-10-11) landed the call on the register-type change pooled across the names (0.042 points in OM-4 s.2's back-test against 0.60 for the all-filer change); hardened in loop 2 by making the index sponsors' holdings follow each name's share count, so that basis is the stump rung
lineage.driver: A period still open at the extract is completed for the reporters not yet in by carrying each from its last report, but that report is stale for the class of reporter whose holdings drift every period at a common rate, so each missing reporter is moved by the drift its own class already shows among those that have reported, the basis a filed back-test criterion selects; flat carry misplaces the unit whose missing reporters are of the drifting class, and any single rate for every missing reporter misplaces the unit whose missing reporters are not.

lineage.fate: portal round 1 (2026-10-11): rubric average 52, determinism QC failed (answer_contradicts_files, golden_wrong): OM-4 s.2 named the filers for the period and filed no completion, so the literal reading counted only the reports on file; the driver also collided with task181 (task446 pre-flight); hardened in loop 1 by filing the estimand and a basis-selection criterion and moving the decisive step to the basis
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is the part of a period's total still held by reporters whose reports have not arrived at the extract; because slow reporters concentrate in some units and not others, it has to be completed reporter by reporter from each one's last report, and reading the arrived reports as the total, or scaling every unit by one aggregate completion share, misstates exactly the units whose holders report late and changes which units cross the threshold.

lineage.niche: an independent ownership-research firm's quarterly crowded-ownership flag on a client watchlist, set from the SEC Form 13F structured data sets while the quarter's filing window is still open, so the flag has to rest on the institutional ownership the completed filing set will show
lineage.driver: One class of holder keeps a fixed fraction of each unit rather than a fixed amount, so when a unit's size changes that class's amount in it moves with it, and the class's common change is a change in the fraction, the same in every unit; completing the holders not yet reported in a still-open period with one amount change per class pooled across units misstates the units whose size moved, carrying every class as a fraction misstates the units whose missing holders keep amounts, and the basis a filed back-test criterion selects moves each missing holder of that class with its own unit's size and the class's change in fraction while every other class keeps its amount.
lineage.stump: A competent solver executes OM-4 literally, sees that the index and ETF sponsors that have filed grew their share holdings while every other register type held flat, grows each of the 129 managers still due by its own type's change pooled across the twelve names, sees that basis beat every other it builds in the September back-test (largest miss about 0.66 points against 1.0 for the all-filer change, 1.4 for flat carry and 2.2 per name), and flags WHII, GLI, JEMS and SAF with OTF at about 79.2; the step that lands it there is treating the sponsors' change as one factor for every name, when an index sponsor holds a fixed slice of each company, so in shares it moves with that name's share count as well as with its creations: OTF issued about 4.6 per cent more shares in October and its sponsors still due, 23 per cent of OTF, took their slice, which the two filed sponsors' OTF holdings show (up about 10.4 per cent against 4.5 pooled), so the basis the filed criterion selects grows each sponsor still due by the change its filed peers show in that name (largest miss about 0.04), which puts OTF at 80.4 and keeps FENN, whose managers still due are multi-strategy funds, at 79.6.

lineage.architecture: v2 (NHS Ellesmoor ICB's 2027 heat resilience grants, the register integrated with the medical examiner offices' logs)
lineage.niche: deaths by date of occurrence for a heat summer, integrated from the death registrations and two medical examiner offices' referral logs that share no key, the deaths a coroner's inquest keeps off the register found by linking the logs to the registrations on name, birth date and date of death
lineage.driver: A count by date of occurrence for a recent window is completed for the units a second body still holds out of the record, read from that body's own log linked to the record on personal identifiers and dates, because the usual completion factor assumes the hold is as rare as in the closed windows it reproduces.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each place's summer 2026 deaths are the deaths on the register plus the deaths the medical examiners referred to the coroner on which an inquest is still open, linked by name, birth date and date of death and placed by the deceased's postcode, because the July heat wave sent the deaths of people found at home to the coroner, so the earlier summers' share registered by October understates the summer and only the referral log names the missing deaths.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst completes each place's registered summer deaths with the earlier summers' share registered by the same point and designates the places whose completed deaths exceed the expected by a tenth; the step that lands it there is treating this summer's unregistered deaths as the usual few, when the coroner holds the heat wave's deaths of people living alone for inquest and Ashwold's are most of them, so Ashwold is left out.
lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-01 at stage 4: the determinism judge returned NOT_DETERMINISTIC with SOLUTION_WRONG, SEND_BACK; Gate H3 failed (the fund's terms counted every death whether registered or not, so linking the logs to the register executed the filed rule), supplementary 5 rode an unfiled version convention and the recommendation prose contradicted itself
